A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same work and retain matching central models and results. v1 ends with references; v2 includes readable Appendices A–C. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical algorithms, recovery guarantees and proofs, without original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical, including its appendices. Randomized query procedures are mathematically analyzed rather than empirically evaluated.

M1.justification: Appendix B introduces recovery from binary membership queries using random sign queries to estimate the normalized value vector and threshold bisection to estimate the attention matrix. Section 6 also modifies noisy recovery to handle zero value-vector coordinates using combined-coordinate probes. The original exact and low-rank procedures remain.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. Binary membership access is added as a theoretical oracle model.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods or baselines. Cited learning algorithms serve as theoretical tools or related work.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets or testing procedures. Changes to oracle assumptions and mathematical query budgets concern the theoretical algorithms.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests or case studies. The expanded noisy-recovery and Hessian arguments are theoretical developments assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, error bars or significance tests. Appendix B's concentration bounds establish theoretical success probabilities.

E6.justification: There are no empirical scores, rankings, result entries or evaluated qualitative findings in either version. New mathematical recovery guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v1's Theorem 6.2 becomes Theorem 6.1 with a margin required only on nonzero value-vector coordinates and an expanded proof; Section 6 also removes its explicit unit-norm input restriction. Appendix B adds a membership-query recovery theorem, query bounds and proof. Appendix C formalizes orthogonal-subspace assumptions, adds Proposition C.2 with a proof, and derives Hessian formulas, substantially extending v1's brief discussion.

C1.justification: The introduction adds efficient approximate parameter recovery from binary membership queries under stronger assumptions, substantially extending the claimed oracle-access scope. The original exact recovery, low-rank recovery, Transformer reduction and general multi-head nonidentifiability claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B explains that binary queries identify the value vector's direction but cannot identify its magnitude. Appendix C expands the earlier speculative Hessian approach with specific obstacles involving unknown subspaces, approximate Hessians and eigenvalue degeneracy. The new Impact Statement also qualifies immediate practical applicability.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies software, hardware measurements, executed training details or code/data release instructions. v2's added probe specifications belong to its new theoretical procedures.

R1.justification: v2 newly cites Maehara and Murota (2011) when discussing noise-robust block diagonalization and required spectral separation. The principal attention-learning, model-extraction and novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The seven main sections retain their order and much of their wording, with localized abstract and introduction edits. Matrix-sensing background and the clipping lemma move to Appendix A, multi-head definitions move to Appendix C, and an Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference main text and reference section, with running headers, a revised title/author block and extensively reflowed equations. Appendices use full-width text. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The binary-query analysis and more explicit multi-head limitations add useful theoretical scope and transparency. However, the new sparse-case proof in Theorem 6.1 reuses clipping for logits in [-1/2, 1/2], although its combined-coordinate probe produces ab(W_ij + W_pj), which can exceed that interval under the stated assumptions. This new proof gap limits the overall gain.
